title: Does ChatGPT Use Bing? What OpenAI and Microsoft Say
metaTitle: Does ChatGPT Use Bing? What the Docs Actually Say
metaDescription: ChatGPT search uses several sources, and Bing is probably one. See what OpenAI and Microsoft confirm, what they don't, and how to check your Bing indexing.
shortAnswer: Partly, but not only. OpenAI says ChatGPT search sometimes partners with other search providers and also runs its own crawler, OAI-SearchBot. Microsoft says the Bing-based grounding infrastructure behind its Web IQ platform already powers ChatGPT. No source says Bing is the sole gate. Index your site in Bing as cheap insurance, but make sure OAI-SearchBot can reach you first.
intro:
The popular answer is a flat yes: ChatGPT search is Bing with a chat window on top. An earlier version of this page said so too. We rewrote it because OpenAI's current documentation no longer supports a flat yes, and acting on the flat version sends marketers to the wrong checklist.

This page separates what OpenAI states, what Microsoft states, what is only inferred, and what to do about each. It is based on public documentation and trial reporting as of October 2026; we have not tested ChatGPT's search pipeline from the inside.

sections.heading: Does ChatGPT search use Bing?
sections.body:
ChatGPT search draws on several sources, and Bing is probably one of them. OpenAI's own help article never names Bing, so "ChatGPT equals Bing" is a hypothesis with partial support, not a documented fact. What is documented is a layered mix.

- **Third-party search providers.** OpenAI's [help article on searching the web](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt) says ChatGPT sometimes partners with other providers and sends them rewritten, targeted queries. It links Microsoft's and Shopify's privacy policies for how those providers handle queries.
- **Partner content.** The [October 2024 launch post](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-search/) says the feature uses third-party providers plus content supplied directly by partners such as news and data companies.
- **OpenAI's own crawler.** OAI-SearchBot [surfaces sites in ChatGPT search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots), and OpenAI says an opted-out site is not shown in ChatGPT search answers, though it can still appear as a navigational link.

A flat "ChatGPT uses Bing" misses two of those three layers. A flat "ChatGPT ignores Bing" misses the first.

sections.heading: What do OpenAI and Microsoft each confirm?
sections.body:
OpenAI confirms third-party providers and its own index. Microsoft confirms that its Bing-built grounding layer powers ChatGPT. Neither publishes which share of queries goes where, so any "ChatGPT is X percent Bing" figure you see is a guess.

The timeline shows why the story keeps changing:

- **October 2024:** OpenAI launches ChatGPT search with third-party providers and partner content ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-search/)).
- **April 2025:** OpenAI's head of ChatGPT testifies in the US v. Google remedies trial. As [NPR reported](https://www.npr.org/2025/04/29/nx-s1-5377353/google-antitrust-remedies-trial-ai), OpenAI found building its own index too slow and expensive, so it sought a third-party provider; Google declined to give access.
- **June 2026:** Microsoft introduces Web IQ and [says the same infrastructure](https://commandline.microsoft.com/grounding-system-agentic-web-engineering-retrieval/) powering Copilot and ChatGPT is now available as a platform. It also names Bing's crawling and indexing as the substrate under grounding.
- **October 2026:** OpenAI's help center describes [indexed and cached web content](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001203-offline-web-search-for-chatgpt-workspaces) that eligible workspaces can use in place of live web search.

Read together: OpenAI has been building its own index while still working with outside providers. The direction looks like more OpenAI and less outsourcing. That is our reading, not a statement from either company.

sections.heading: Why does Bing indexing still matter?
sections.body:
Bing indexing is cheap insurance, not a ranking lever. At least one documented ChatGPT input appears to rest on an index you can check and fix in an afternoon. The fixes also help Copilot and Bing itself.

Three concrete reasons to bother:

1. **Overlap with the provider layer.** Microsoft says its grounding infrastructure powers ChatGPT and names Bing's crawl and index as its base. If ChatGPT queries that layer, a page Bing cannot find cannot be returned from it.
2. **Link-only appearances.** OpenAI's [publisher FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12627856-publishers-and-developers-faq) says that if it learns of a blocked page's URL from a third-party provider or from crawling other pages, it may show just the link and title in ChatGPT Atlas. Being known to outside indexes shapes how you appear even when you restrict OpenAI's own bot.
3. **Freshness.** Microsoft's [AI Performance announcement](https://blogs.bing.com/webmaster/2026/2/Introducing-AI-Performance-in-Bing-Webmaster-Tools-Public-Preview/) says IndexNow keeps content fresh across search and AI experiences by notifying participating engines of changes.

Two limits matter just as much. Bing indexing does not make OpenAI's crawler visit you. And Bing's AI Performance report counts citations in Copilot, Bing's AI summaries and select partners; the announcement does not list ChatGPT.

In AEOeye's crawler access study (October 2026), only 1 of 384 sites blocked Bingbot from the homepage (reddit.com), while 16 of 384 (4.2%) blocked OAI-SearchBot, including 11 of 38 publishers. You are very unlikely to be blocking Bingbot. Whether Bing has indexed you is a separate question. [Our full data is public](/blog/ai-crawler-user-agent-directory).

sections.heading: How do you check and improve your Bing indexing?
sections.body:
Verify your site in Bing Webmaster Tools, inspect your key pages, and push changes with IndexNow. It takes about an hour and costs nothing. Do it in this order:

1. **Open and verify.** Microsoft's [getting-started checklist](https://www.bing.com/webmasters/help/getting-started-checklist-66a806de) says the account is free and you can sign in with a Microsoft, Google or Facebook login, then add and verify each site.
2. **Submit a sitemap.** Bing accepts XML sitemaps and index files, Atom, RSS 2.0 and plain text lists of URLs.
3. **Inspect five money pages.** The [URL Inspection tool](https://www.bing.com/webmasters/help/url-inspection-55a30305) reports when a URL was discovered, crawled and indexed. Its Live URL view shows what Bingbot sees, which exposes content hidden behind scripts or bot protection.
4. **Turn on IndexNow.** The [protocol](https://www.indexnow.org/documentation) needs a key file on your domain, accepts up to 10,000 URLs per request, and shares submissions with all participating engines. An HTTP 200 only means the request arrived, not that the page is indexed.
5. **Check both bots at your firewall.** OpenAI says to [allow OAI-SearchBot and its published IP ranges](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt) at your host or CDN. Do the same for Bingbot.

![Hands typing code on a laptop keyboard](https://images.pexels.com/photos/5474295/pexels-photo-5474295.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

OpenAI's offline-search page lists the usual reasons content is missing from its index: [robots.txt blocks, CDN bot-blocking, logins, script-heavy pages and new or low-signal pages](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001203-offline-web-search-for-chatgpt-workspaces). Rule each one out for Bingbot too.

sections.heading: What else does ChatGPT weigh once your page is indexed?
sections.body:
Once a page is retrievable, ChatGPT ranks it on factors OpenAI does not publish, and placement is never guaranteed. What independent research shows is a pronounced preference for third-party sources over brand-owned pages.

A September 2025 [arXiv study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08919) compared AI search engines with Google across controlled experiments and found a systematic, overwhelming bias towards earned media (third-party, authoritative sources) over brand-owned and social content. It also found that the AI engines differ from each other in domain diversity, freshness and sensitivity to phrasing.

Our position follows from that. Chasing Bing alone optimises the retrieval layer and ignores the selection layer. Three moves matter more once indexing is fixed:

- **Be the direct answer.** Lead each section with the answer. Microsoft's Web IQ post describes [returning the most relevant passages rather than whole documents](https://commandline.microsoft.com/grounding-system-agentic-web-engineering-retrieval/).
- **Earn independent mentions.** Reviews, comparisons and credible third-party coverage are the source type the study found AI engines favour.
- **Keep facts consistent.** The same product name, price and claims on every page and profile.

We cover the selection logic in [how ChatGPT chooses its sources](/answers/how-does-chatgpt-choose-sources) and the content side in [ChatGPT SEO](/blog/chatgpt-seo). The three OpenAI bots, and what each one does with your site, are in [Does ChatGPT use my website?](/answers/does-chatgpt-use-my-website)

![A woman shopping online on her laptop in a home setting](https://images.pexels.com/photos/5585793/pexels-photo-5585793.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: How do you check whether ChatGPT actually names you?
sections.body:
Ask ChatGPT the questions your buyers ask, with search on, and read which sources it cites. Your Bing position cannot tell you this; only the answers can.

Run five unbranded questions such as "best [category] for [use case]". For each, note whether you are named, which competitors are named instead, and which pages are cited. Repeat on another day: OpenAI notes that [the same question may yield different answers](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed).

AEOeye's [free audit](/) does this for three unbranded buyer questions on ChatGPT and shows the full answers and the competitors named instead. It is a starting check, not a monitoring service; if you need daily tracking across hundreds of prompts, dedicated trackers cover that.

keyTakeaways: OpenAI documents third-party search providers plus its own OAI-SearchBot index; it does not name Bing in its help article.
Microsoft says its Bing-built grounding infrastructure already powers Copilot and ChatGPT, so Bing indexing is useful insurance.
Neither company publishes a share of queries per source; treat any percentage claim as a guess.
The documented control is OAI-SearchBot: allow it, and allow OpenAI's published IP ranges at your CDN.
Verify in Bing Webmaster Tools, inspect key URLs, and turn on IndexNow; then test real buyer questions in ChatGPT.

faqs.q: Does ChatGPT use Google instead of Bing?
faqs.a: OpenAI has not published a provider list. In testimony reported by NPR, OpenAI said Google declined to give it access to its search. We found no OpenAI documentation naming Google as a provider, so we do not claim it. What OpenAI does document is third-party providers in general, its own crawler and partner content.

faqs.q: Do I need Bing Webmaster Tools to appear in ChatGPT?
faqs.a: No documented rule requires it. OpenAI's stated requirement is that OAI-SearchBot is not blocked and that your host or CDN allows OpenAI's published IP ranges. Bing Webmaster Tools is a low-cost addition because Microsoft says its Bing-based grounding layer powers ChatGPT, and it also helps in Copilot and Bing.

faqs.q: Will blocking Bingbot remove me from ChatGPT?
faqs.a: OpenAI does not document that. Microsoft says the grounding layer behind ChatGPT builds on Bing's crawl, so a Bingbot block could remove you from that input while OAI-SearchBot access still keeps you eligible through OpenAI's own index. Unless you have a licensing reason, blocking Bingbot costs more than it protects.

faqs.q: Is ranking well in Bing the same as ranking in ChatGPT?
faqs.a: No. Bing rankings describe Bing's results. ChatGPT blends several sources, rewrites the question into its own queries and then selects passages by criteria OpenAI has not published. Use Bing position as one input and check ChatGPT's actual answers for your buyer questions.
